title: Studying with Gruenberg, Howard Murphy and Wagner
summary: Chicago Musical College study in 1937, then Teachers College and private work with Bernard Wagner.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What is involved is not so much a lifting, but a spark, a stimulation. If they were bored with it, they wouldn't listen to it. I think they were stimulated by it, as I was, which caused me to go and study with a guy named Louis Gruenberg while we were at the Black Hawk in Chicago. This was at the Chicago Music College, 1937.
Then I came back to New York and

I studied with Howard Murphy. I got Tootie Camarata to come up there too. That went on for a couple of years and I was so in love with the Russians at that time, there were a lot of immigrants around 180th Street, a whole Russian colony up there at that time, and some of them were pupils of Rimsky-Korsakov, so I wanted that; but that didn't last very long. It wasn't working. So I stopped that.
Then I went back again to Teacher's College and eventually to Bernard Wagner over at Julliard. I didn't matriculate at Julliard, but I studied with this guy privately.
This was from 1939 up through '45, I guess.
